collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The village could block the lagoon mouth with stakes against raiders: build the wall, or keep the lagoon open for fishing.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has a plan: drive sharpened stakes across the mouth of the lagoon, so no raider's canoe can get in at night. (friend) points out that the fishers' canoes would not get in or out either, and the lagoon fish would have nowhere to go. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village builds the wall, with a narrow gap that can be closed with a log at night. It takes a month. The fishers complain about the gap every single day. But the village sleeps better.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village leaves the lagoon open and puts more watchers on the headlands instead. (subject) is not convinced, and checks the lagoon mouth every night before bed. Nothing comes through. Nothing has to.
